metaDescription: Seven 20V cordless pole hedge trimmers compared by reach, blade length, head angles and weight, so you can trim tall hedges safely from the ground.
expertTake: The Alloyman 16 inch telescoping trimmer is the best all-round pick because it combines a 3/4 inch cut capacity, an 8 foot pole and two 4.0Ah batteries in a kit. The BLACK+DECKER pole trimmer is the established-brand choice for modest hedges. If your hedge is more than about ten feet tall or your arms tire holding eight pounds overhead, skip the pole trimmer and hire a pro or use a ladder-safe platform tool.
introParagraphs: A pole hedge trimmer puts a short hedge blade on the end of an extension shaft so you can reach tall hedges from the ground. The trade is leverage: the same blade that feels light in a handheld trimmer becomes tiring when held at the end of a long pole.

This guide explains how reach claims are calculated, why head angle and weight balance matter more than blade length, and where the cutting capacity of a pole trimmer runs out. Check the picks above for a quick shortlist, then read the reviews below for the tradeoffs on each.

products.name: Alloyman 20V Telescoping Pole Hedge Trimmer, 16 Inch Blade
products.description:
Alloyman's trimmer is the most complete kit in this group. A 16 inch dual-action blade with a 3/4 inch cutting capacity can handle typical hedge growth, which is more than the 7/16 inch capacity of the BLACK+DECKER pole model. Two 4.0Ah batteries and a charger mean a long reach job is not cut short by a flat pack.

The telescoping pole extends to about 8 feet, and folds shorter for storage. At around 8 pounds, it is heavier than the 6 pound goodjob, so the shoulder strap and the rotating rear handle matter. The 1,400 strokes per minute is a modest rate, and it cuts cleanly on soft growth but will not slice with the speed of a handheld unit.

A brand like this lacks the support of larger names, so confirm battery availability. Oil the blade after each session, retract the pole before storing it and keep the batteries indoors in winter. The weight is the main limit, not the power.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want the best capacity-to-runtime balance in a pole trimmer kit.
pros: 3/4 in capacity leads the pole trimmers here
Two 4.0Ah batteries support long reach sessions
Shoulder strap and rotating rear handle ease the load
Telescoping pole folds down for storage
cons: About 8 lb is heavy to hold overhead
1,400 SPM is slower than handheld trimmers
Less established support than the largest brands

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX 18 Inch Pole Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER pole trimmer is the conventional choice for light work. Its 18 inch dual-action blade cuts less aggressively than the 3/4 inch Alloyman, with a 7/16 inch rated capacity. That is enough for new growth on soft hedges but not for older stems, and you should trim often rather than letting a hedge grow out.

The pole is fiberglass, which does not rust, and extends so the trim height reaches about 11 feet, a figure that combines the pole with your height. At 7.7 pounds it is lighter than the Alloyman. The 180 degree head has five positions, and that helps with hedge tops.

The real draw is brand support. The 20V MAX battery system is widely stocked, so replacement packs are easy to find. Keep the blade oiled, and store the pole retracted. If you need more capacity, the Alloyman is the better cutter.
products.bestFor: Light hedge maintenance by buyers who want a well-supported brand and battery platform.
pros: Rust-proof fiberglass pole sections last outdoors
18 in blade balances reach and control
180 degree head offers five angle positions
Battery platform is widely supported
cons: 7/16 in capacity is the lowest in this group
Not suited to thick or woody growth

products.name: SEYVUM 20V Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer, 20 Inch Blade

specList.label: Reach
specList.value: Up to 15 ft with user height

products.description:
SEYVUM gives the longest blade on a pole trimmer in this roundup, a 20 inch dual-action unit. A longer blade covers more hedge per pass, which cuts the number of strokes on flat faces, but it also raises the leverage you fight at the end of the pole.

The pole runs 7.5 to 9 feet and the head tilts 0 to 135 degrees in six positions. The 15 foot reach claim adds the user's height to the pole length, so treat it as total reach rather than the pole alone. Two 2.0Ah batteries at about 25 minutes each give modest runtime, which is less than the Alloyman's pair of 4.0Ah packs.

The shoulder strap spreads the weight, and non-slip grips help control. As a newer brand, spare battery availability is worth checking. Oil the blade after use and keep the pole clean and dry.
products.bestFor: Long, flat hedge faces where a wide blade saves passes.
pros: 20 in blade is the longest in this group
Six head positions cover tops and sides
Pole extends to 9 ft before adding your height
Shoulder strap spreads load across the shoulder
cons: Long blade is harder to steer at the end of a pole
Newer brand with less certain long-term support

products.name: YDlawn 20V Cordless Pole Hedge Trimmer, 15 Ft Reach
products.description:
YDlawn pairs the longest blade on a pole trimmer, 22 inches, with a 15 foot total reach claim. The reach combines the 8 foot pole with your height, so the practical trim height is a few feet lower. For tall screens this is the longest reach among the kits.

It weighs 8.8 pounds, the heaviest in the group, and the 22 inch blade at the end of a pole amplifies that load. The 5/8 inch capacity is below the Alloyman's 3/4 inch. Two 4.0Ah batteries give long runtime, matching the Alloyman and SEESII kits.

The detachable pole lets you use the head as a handheld trimmer, which adds flexibility. As a smaller brand, support is the question mark. Keep the blade oiled and the pole joints clean so they do not seize.
products.bestFor: Tall hedges where maximum reach and a wide blade are the priority, and weight is tolerable.
pros: Highest total reach claim in this lineup
22 in blade covers a lot of hedge per pass
Two 4.0Ah batteries support long sessions
Detachable pole lets it double as a handheld
cons: 8.8 lb is the heaviest here and tiring overhead

products.name: goodjob 20V Pole Hedge Trimmer, 18 Inch Blade
products.description:
goodjob's trimmer is the lightest in the roundup, at about 6 pounds. That is two pounds less than the Alloyman or YDlawn, which is a noticeable gap when holding a pole overhead. The 18 inch blade has a 5/8 inch capacity, which is adequate for neatly maintained hedges.

The head rotates 150 degrees and locks in 11 positions, the most angle choices in this group. That helps with flat tops and vertical faces from one standing position. The telescopic pole runs 6.3 to 8.6 feet.

Two 2,000mAh batteries give about 30 minutes each by the listing's own figure, which is modest. The tradeoff for lighter weight is smaller batteries and a lesser brand. Oil the blade and avoid overextending the pole while it is energized.
products.bestFor: Users who prioritize low weight and flexible head angles for neatly kept hedges.
pros: About 6 lb is the lightest pole trimmer here
11 head positions give precise angle choices
Dual safety switches prevent accidental starts
Telescopic pole stores compactly
cons: Unproven long-term support from a small brand

products.name: SEESII 20V Pole Hedge Trimmer, 16 Inch Blade, 8.5 Ft Reach
products.description:
SEESII sits in the middle: a 16 inch blade, 7.6 pounds and two 4.0Ah batteries. It is about half a pound lighter than the Alloyman at 8 pounds, with the same battery capacity but a smaller 5/8 inch capacity.

The pole telescopes from 7 to 8.5 feet, and the 135 degree head offers six positions. A shoulder strap helps balance. The detachable pole lets you use it more flexibly, which helps for short, accessible hedges.

It is a sound choice for mid-size yards where you want a full kit. Like the other small brands, check battery availability. Keep the blade oiled and store the pole shortened.
products.bestFor: Medium hedges where a full kit and moderate weight are the priority.
pros: Two 4.0Ah batteries and fast charger in the box
7.6 lb is lighter than the Alloyman and YDlawn
Detachable pole adds handheld flexibility
Six head positions cover most angles
cons: 5/8 in capacity trails the Alloyman's 3/4 in
16 in blade needs more passes on long hedges

products.name: Grasstigon 20V Pole Hedge Trimmer for DeWalt Batteries (Tool Only)
products.description:
Grasstigon is a bare tool for DeWalt 20V MAX batteries, with an 18 inch dual-action blade and a 14 foot reach claim. Because it uses packs you already own, it lowers the cost of getting a pole trimmer if you are a DeWalt owner.

The 14 foot figure is a total reach claim that includes your height, so the pole itself is shorter. With no battery included, the weight depends on the pack you fit, and large packs add noticeable load at the end of a pole. It lacks the kit convenience of the Alloyman or SEESII.

As a third-party tool on a DeWalt interface, there is no shared warranty. Check the pack seats firmly and avoid using damaged batteries. Oil the blade and keep the head clean.
products.bestFor: DeWalt 20V MAX owners who want a reaching trimmer without buying another battery.
pros: Reuses DeWalt 20V MAX batteries you already own
Long reach claim suits tall hedges
Adjustable head covers tops and sides
Dual-action blade lowers vibration
cons: Third-party tool on a DeWalt pack has no shared warranty

buyingCriteria.explanation: Reach figures on pole trimmers usually add your height to the pole length, so a 15 foot claim might be an 8 foot pole and a person standing at 7 feet of arm and body reach. Buyers who assume 15 feet of pole end up disappointed when a hedge top sits out of range. Measure your hedge and subtract your standing reach. The YDlawn lists 15 feet and the Grasstigon 14 feet, while the Alloyman lists an 8 foot pole.

At the end of a pole, weight is multiplied by leverage, so an 8 pound trimmer feels far heavier than 8 pounds in your hand. Strap, handle placement and balance matter more than pure weight. For most users, under 7 pounds is comfortable and over 8 pounds tires quickly. The goodjob at about 6 pounds is lightest, and the YDlawn at 8.8 pounds is heaviest.

Pole trimmers carry smaller heads than handhelds, and capacity ranges from 7/16 to 3/4 inch. Stems beyond the capacity stall the blade, and overhead you cannot lean into the cut. Trim often to keep growth thin. The Alloyman lists 3/4 inch, the SEESII, goodjob and YDlawn list 5/8 inch, and the BLACK+DECKER lists 7/16 inch.

A pivoting head lets you cut flat tops, vertical sides and low edges from one stance, which reduces the need to reposition the pole. More positions mean finer angle choices, but each lock is another moving part. The goodjob offers 11 positions across 150 degrees, the SEESII and SEYVUM offer six across 135 degrees and the BLACK+DECKER offers five across 180 degrees.

Heavy overhead work empties batteries fast, so capacity matters. Two 4.0Ah packs give double the energy of two 2.0Ah packs, which means you can finish long jobs rather than stopping to charge. The Alloyman, YDlawn and SEESII include 4.0Ah pairs, while the SEYVUM and goodjob include 2.0Ah-class packs.

A pole trimmer with a long metal or carbon shaft can conduct electricity if it touches a live line. Keep at least 10 feet of clearance from overhead lines, and do not use any pole tool near them. Always wear eye protection and a hard hat when cutting overhead, since clippings and branches fall onto you.

specDecoder.meaning: The highest point you can trim, usually the pole length plus your standing height and arm reach. It is not the pole length alone.
specDecoder.watchFor: Listings like the YDlawn's 15 feet and Grasstigon's 14 feet include the user's height, so the pole itself is shorter.

specDecoder.meaning: The thickest stem the blade gap will accept. Stems above this stall the motor or are not cut at all.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Alloyman lists 3/4 inch while the BLACK+DECKER lists 7/16 inch, a large practical difference.

specDecoder.meaning: How many full cycles the blade makes per minute. Higher rates leave cleaner cuts on soft stems.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Alloyman and goodjob list about 1,400, which is slower than many handhelds, and these are no-load figures.

specDecoder.meaning: The range through which the cutting head can be tilted and locked, which sets how many cutting angles you can reach.
specDecoder.watchFor: More positions look better on paper but only help if the lock holds under vibration.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. Double the Ah means roughly double the runtime under the same load.
specDecoder.watchFor: Pairs of 2.0Ah and 4.0Ah packs are both described as 'dual battery' kits, though runtime differs by double.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and pole design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated pole length and total reach, separating pole length from user height. We favored telescoping, detachable designs that fold down. The YDlawn leads on total reach claims and the Alloyman on pole length.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade length and cut capacity. The Alloyman's 3/4 inch capacity leads, with the BLACK+DECKER's 7/16 inch lowest. Capacity weighed more than blade length because stalling overhead is hard to fix.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and balance
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated weights, straps and handle layout. The goodjob's 6 pounds led and the YDlawn's 8.8 pounds trailed. Overhead work magnifies every pound.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared included batteries and weighed total stored energy. Kits with two 4.0Ah packs scored above two 2.0Ah kits.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered platform size and warranty coverage. The BLACK+DECKER's well-stocked platform scored highest, and tool-only third-party units on DeWalt packs scored lowest.

howToChoose.intro: Height sets how much pole you need.

cards.label: Long blade (20 to 22 in)
cards.text: Covers more hedge per pass, but the leverage at the pole tip raises fatigue. The SEYVUM at 20 inches and YDlawn at 22 inches fall here.

cards.label: Short blade (16 to 18 in)
cards.text: Easier to control and lighter overhead, but needs more passes. The Alloyman, SEESII, goodjob and BLACK+DECKER fall here.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers do better with a short blade for control, and long blades suit flat, uniform faces only.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Real reach, enough capacity and a battery that lasts. Tall privacy hedges mean sustained overhead work, so weight and runtime matter most.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Alloyman combines 3/4 inch capacity and two 4.0Ah packs, while the YDlawn extends reach to a claimed 15 feet at the cost of 8.8 pounds.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You trim tall hedges often. The Alloyman gives the strongest capacity and runtime, and a platform with a bigger battery range keeps packs available.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a small hedge once or twice a year. The goodjob or BLACK+DECKER do that job, and the Grasstigon makes sense if you own DeWalt packs.

maintenance.why: Sap and debris cause drag and rust. A light oil keeps the blades moving smoothly.
Dirt in telescoping joints makes them seize. Wipe them and keep them dry.
Vibration can loosen the angle lock. A slipping head is both annoying and unsafe.
Lithium packs age fastest empty or hot. Store them indoors.
Dull or chipped blades tear stems and strain the motor. Replace damaged blades.

faq.q: How tall a hedge can a pole trimmer reach?
faq.a: Total reach is the pole length plus your standing reach. An 8 foot pole typically gives a trim height near 12 feet for an average adult. Always check how the manufacturer calculates reach.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a pole hedge trimmer?
faq.a: Kits from small brands cost less, and established brands cost more. Count batteries in the total, and spend more if you trim often or need capacity.
They range from about 6 to nearly 9 pounds, and the weight is amplified by leverage. A shoulder strap helps, and short sessions with breaks reduce fatigue.

faq.q: Is a pole trimmer as powerful as a handheld?
faq.a: Usually not. Smaller heads and lower cut capacities mean they suit soft growth. Use loppers or a handheld for thicker stems.

faq.q: Is it safe near power lines?
faq.a: Keep at least 10 feet away from overhead lines, and do not use a pole tool near them. Long shafts can conduct electricity.

faq.q: Can I use the head without the pole?
faq.a: Some models, such as the YDlawn and SEESII, have detachable poles, so the head can serve as a small handheld trimmer. Check the listing before buying.
